## What I did

**1. Editor was a dead end (`/editor` → blog and other pages)**

The drawer linked only personas/library/rubric/analysis/apparatus/pricing; Settings and Docs were buried in the account menu. Blog, FAQ, Downloads, Terms, and Privacy existed **only** in the landing-page footer. Added a "Elsewhere in the paper" section plus a Settings entry to the drawer (`src/routes/editor/index.tsx:875`).

**2. Voice — two real bugs, both fixed**

- **The narration gate was wrong.** `synthesize()` gated on `hasConfiguredVoiceProvider()`, which returns true for *transcription-only* providers. So with (say) Anthropic for the room + Google for dictation, the gate passed, narration resolved to `null`, it threw `PROVIDER_ERROR`, and the hosted fallback was **never reached**. Now gates on narration actually resolving (`src/utils/speech.ts:236`). Regression test in `ai-client.test.ts` pins the distinction.
- **Autoplay blocked every press.** `audio.play()` ran after the synthesis round-trip, by which time Chrome's ~5s user-activation window had expired → `NotAllowedError` every time, indistinguishable from a broken feature. Added `unlockSpeechPlayback()`, which spends the click synchronously on a silent clip to unlock the shared element, and a `NotAllowedError` branch that says "your browser blocked playback" instead of blaming the API key.

**3. Sign-in no longer routes you to `/editor`**

`auth/callback` now returns to `/`. Note: the callback fix alone wouldn't have worked — `src/routes/index.tsx` *also* bounced anyone with a stored brief straight to `/editor`, so the home page was unreachable for any returning writer. Removed that too. The landing page's existing "skip to the desk" button still gets you to `/editor`.

**4. Chat composer redesign**

New `src/components/ui/chat-composer.tsx` + `.composer` styles: one bordered surface holding the text, mic, and send key, with the focus ring on the whole card. Auto-growing textarea, Enter sends / Shift+Enter newline (⌘↩ still works), IME-safe. Dictation now lands **in the draft** rather than in a second review textarea, and recording runs in the toolbar so it doesn't hide what you already typed. Wired into the interview; "Show me what you have" moved into the composer's action slot.

## Page layout, rethought

**A real ruler** — `src/components/editor/page-ruler.tsx`, mounted directly above the page so its markers sit on the actual margins. Shaded ends are the margins, pale middle is the live text column, same relationship Word draws. Drag a marker and the manuscript reflows under your hand, with a live rem readout while you drag.

- Pointer capture rather than document listeners, so a drag that leaves the window still ends cleanly.
- Keyboard parity: arrows nudge one step, Shift+arrow four, Home zeroes it. Exposed as `role="slider"` with proper `aria-valuenow`/`valuetext`.
- Arrow keys needed `sync$` — `preventDefault()` inside an async QRL runs after the browser has already scrolled. Tab is deliberately left alone so the handles stay tabbable.
- A minimum 8rem text column stops you dragging the margins into each other.

**Margins are now independent left/right.** `LayoutSettings` gained `marginLeft`/`marginRight`, and `resolveMargins` now chains three generations of the setting — coarse `margin` preset → symmetric `marginX` → independent edges — so documents saved before the ruler existed still open to the page their writer chose. Six tests in `page-margins.test.ts` pin that chain, including that `0` is honoured rather than treated as absent. The popover sliders became Left/Right/Top/Bottom.

**PDF export**, in two places: the File menu and the layout popover (page setup and "print it" belong together). It prints the existing standalone HTML export, which already carries the writer's margins as real `@page` rules and page numbers via `counter(page)` — a print engine is the one renderer guaranteed to honour those. No new dependency, and the text stays selectable and searchable, which canvas-based approaches (html2canvas/jsPDF) lose by rasterising.

**Two bugs found along the way**, both silent:
- The export payload never included `props.layout`, so every export fell back to `DEFAULT_LAYOUT` — a writer who set their margins got someone else's page. Now fixed, and payload assembly is shared via `src/utils/folio-export.ts` so the File menu and the layout tool cannot drift into producing different documents.
- Export read stored content only in one path; the live-editor handshake is now shared too, so an export never drops the last sentence you typed.

**Removed as you asked:** the "The Manuscript" header bar, both `edit` buttons, and the bottom footer bar. The dead `runningHeaderText` went with them. The running-header and page-number toggles still work — `exchange.ts` derives those independently for export, so nothing was lost there.

## Caveat

I could not visually verify the ruler — the Chrome extension isn't connected, and the editor only renders after client hydration so I can't check it via curl either. Typecheck, lint, and build pass, but the drag feel and marker alignment need your eyes.

Also: the ruler is horizontal only. Top/bottom margins remain slider-only in the popover. Word has a vertical ruler too — say the word and I'll add it.

---
twyne: minor
---

The page is yours to set, and the desk stops being a dead end.

**A ruler you can drag.** Page layout was a popover of rem sliders, which asks a writer to translate "3.25 rem" into a picture of their page. There is now a Word-style ruler above the manuscript, spanning exactly the page it describes: the shaded ends are the margins, the pale middle is the live text column, and dragging a marker moves the edge of the text with the draft reflowing under your hand. Margins are independent left and right rather than one symmetric value, the arrow keys drive the markers for anyone not using a mouse, and documents saved before the ruler still open to the page their writer chose.

**Export as PDF.** From the File menu or straight from the layout tool, since page setup and printing belong together. The PDF carries your own margins and page numbers, and the text stays selectable and searchable. Two silent bugs went with it: exports were dropping the layout entirely and quietly falling back to the default page, and one export path read the saved copy rather than the open editor, so the last sentence you typed could go missing.

**Reading aloud actually works.** Two separate faults each broke it on their own. Narration was gated on having *any* voice-capable provider, so a writer running an LLM for the room and Google for dictation resolved to no narrator at all, failed, and never reached the hosted fallback. And playback was requested after synthesis had already returned, by which point the browser no longer considered the press a user gesture and refused to make noise — every attempt failed identically. A blocked playback now says the browser blocked it rather than blaming your API key.

**One place to write from.** The message composer is a single surface holding the text, the microphone and the send key, instead of three stacked controls. Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line, the box grows with what you write, and dictation lands in the draft you are looking at rather than in a second box asking you to approve your own words twice.

**The editor is no longer a one-way door.** The blog, the manual, the FAQ, the press room, preferences, terms and privacy were reachable only from the landing page footer — so once you were at the desk, you were stuck there. They are all in the drawer now. Signing in also stops redirecting you to the editor, and the front page stops bouncing anyone who has ever filed a brief, which together had made the landing page unreachable for returning writers.

The manuscript's decorative header and footer bars have been removed from the page.

---
twyne: minor
---

Every folio is its own workspace, and the interview thinks out loud.

**Folio-scoped sync.** Notes, replies, suggestions, rubric results and the room's analysis are now stored and indexed per folio rather than per writer, so switching pieces switches the whole editorial context instead of carrying the last piece's marginalia into the next one. Rows written before the change carry no folio and are still readable.

**The interview streams.** Dossier interview turns arrive as they are generated, with the model's reasoning and its answer tracked as separate phases so the thinking can be shown while it happens without leaking into the answer. Streams are persisted, so a reload mid-question does not lose the turn.

**Choosing a model is searchable.** Provider catalogues are read from models.dev, and the model pickers in settings are type-to-filter rather than a long unsorted list. Adds a relay for Tinker's OpenAI-compatible endpoint so Tinker models can be used as a BYOK provider.

content.text:
**Released: `twyne@0.6.0`** — https://github.com/Diogenesoftoronto/twyne/releases/tag/twyne%400.6.0

All four artifacts published (web bundle + Linux/macOS/Windows desktop). Release workflow green across all jobs.

## The two things you asked for last

**Tab now works.** New `Indent` extension (`src/components/editor/extensions/indent.ts`). Tab already nested list items — the gap was everywhere else, where it fell through to the browser and moved focus *out of your draft*. It now indents the current block one stop, Shift+Tab takes it back, and lists and tables keep their existing behaviour. The indent is a persisted node attribute rendered as a margin, so it survives the HTML round-trip into exports and the PDF rather than being screen-only. Escape releases focus, since binding Tab would otherwise be a keyboard trap.

A test caught a real inconsistency mid-way: the keymap routed lists correctly, but the raw `indent()` command didn't — a toolbar button or multi-block selection would have pushed a list item's paragraph away from its own bullet. Guarded in both places now. Six tests cover the round-trip, clamping, multi-paragraph selection, and the list guard.

**Lists were genuinely broken.** Tailwind's preflight strips `list-style` and padding from every `ul`/`ol`, and nothing restored it for the manuscript — so bullets and numbers rendered *invisibly*. Pressing "list" appeared to do nothing at all. Restored for the editor only (the reset still holds for app chrome), with markers cycling by depth (disc→circle→square, decimal→alpha→roman) and matching rules added to the export stylesheet so the PDF agrees with the screen.

## Release mechanics

Two bump files → `bumpy version` → 0.5.0 → 0.6.0, plus the empty-bump-file commit the pre-push hook requires (matching the pattern in your history). Three commits on `main` and the `twyne@0.6.0` tag.

I also added `.devenv/` to `.gitignore` — that 1.6MB nix build cache was untracked and would otherwise have gone into the release.

## Two things to know

**The `CI` workflow failed, but not because of this work.** It dies in the Dagger module loader with `ReferenceError: SOURCE_IGNORE is not defined` — the `@argument({ ignore: SOURCE_IGNORE })` decorator in `.dagger/src/index.ts` is evaluated in a context that can't see the module-scope constant. The 0.5.0 CI run failed identically. Locally, all 51 test files pass individually, and `bun run build` reports type-checked and lint-checked clean. Worth fixing separately.

**The release contains substantial work I didn't write** — folio-scoped sync, the streaming interview, models.dev pickers, the Tinker relay — which was already in your working tree. I wrote its changelog entry from reading the code, not from having built it, so check that wording reads true to you. It's in `CHANGELOG.md` under 0.6.0 and editable without a re-release.

Still unverified visually: the ruler, the composer, and the list rendering. The Chrome extension isn't connected, so I could never actually look at any of it.
